name: Pleione
description: A star 135 parsecs away, 6.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: radius 5.695 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 94.567 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.602) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 117.096 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 5.695 x 134.84/117.096 = 6.558 solar radii (luminosity 125.4)

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: effective temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.495)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.82 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 3 published values span log g 3.346 to 4.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.3% of the centre brightness

distance.source: Adopted Pleiades model geometry: normal depth 136.7 pc, 0.7 pc beyond the dust model's normal-depth reference of 136.0 pc along ICRS RA 56.67978318 deg, Dec 24.10845447 deg. Individual bright-star depths and their common plane are assumptions; measured sky positions, observed photometry and published parallax/facts remain separate.

text.card: A star 135 parsecs away, 6.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 125 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,548 K, so 6.558 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 17851: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Pleione (star)
quotes.card: It has the variable star designation BU Tauri and the Flamsteed designation 28 Tauri.
quotes.introduction: Pleione is located close on the sky to the brighter star Atlas, so is difficult for stargazers to distinguish with the naked eye despite being a fifth magnitude star.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66529975427235712 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
